title: Strict and homotopy Segal conventions for Reedy fibrant simplicial spaces
statement:
Use simplicial sets, Kan complexes, homotopy Segal spaces and their path-model homotopy categories from [lem-coef-segal-dk-diagonal-equivalence], vertical Reedy fibrancy from [lem-coef-bisimplicial-reedy-division-calculus], and strict-product Segal spaces and their strict-fiber homotopy categories from [def-coef-segal-space]. Let $X:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{sSet}$ be a vertically Reedy fibrant homotopy Segal space. Then $X$ is a Reedy fibrant Segal space in the strict-product convention: for every $n\geq2$, the consecutive-edge map
$$X_n\longrightarrow S_n(X)=X_1\times_{X_0}\cdots\times_{X_0}X_1$$
is a weak homotopy equivalence, where the $n$ factors match the target $d_0$ of one edge to the source $d_1$ of the next. For every pair of vertices $x,y\in(X_0)_0$, the constant-path map
$$X_1\times_{X_0^2}\{(x,y)\}\longrightarrow\operatorname{hofib}_{(x,y)}((d_1,d_0):X_1\to X_0^2)$$
is a weak homotopy equivalence. The induced bijections on $\pi_0$, together with the identity on objects, form an isomorphism from the strict-fiber homotopy category to the path-model homotopy category $hX$: they send the class of a strict arrow $f$ to the class of that same arrow with constant endpoint path, preserve the identities from $s_0$, and preserve the compositions from the consecutive-edge comparison and $d_1:X_2\to X_1$. Consequently the unions of components of $X_1$ representing isomorphisms in these two categories are the same simplicial subset.

source.place: Rezk, Sections 4.1 and 5.1–5.5 (strict-product Segal condition and strict mapping fibers). The comparison with the explicitly specified path models is an agent-supplied consequence, not a verbatim theorem of Rezk; no matching Stacks tag. Read online 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Regard $X$ as a bisimplicial set with outer coordinate first. For every outer simplicial subset $A\subseteq\Delta^n$, division gives a Kan fibration $X_n=\Delta^n\backslash X\to A\backslash X$: apply the arbitrary-monomorphism criterion to $A\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ and $X\to *$. The identification is explicit: a map $\Delta^n\boxtimes\Delta^q\to X$ is determined by the image of the pair of identity simplices, an element of $(X_n)_q$. Taking $A=\varnothing$ makes every $X_n$ Kan. For $A=\partial\Delta^n$, a map from the boundary is exactly a compatible family on proper faces; hence $A\backslash X$ is the outer matching object and this is Reedy fibrancy in the strict convention. For $A=\{0,\ldots,n\}$, the union of the vertices, restriction is the all-vertices Kan fibration $v_n:X_n\to X_0^{n+1}$; in particular $v_1=(d_1,d_0)$.

source.place: Rezk Sections 4.1 and 5.1–5.7; agent expansion of the strict/path comparison using Kerodon 0329 and 032B (not Stacks tags)

proof.text: Let $G_r\subseteq\Delta^r$ be the union of the consecutive edges, with $G_1=\Delta^1$. Its edges meet only at consecutive common vertices; thus degreewise the division object $G_r\backslash X$ is $S_r=X_1\times_{X_0}\cdots\times_{X_0}X_1$, with matching $d_0$ then $d_1$. This identification sends restriction $X_r\to G_r\backslash X$ to the stated Segal map. The monomorphisms $\varnothing\hookrightarrow G_r$, $\{r\}\hookrightarrow G_r$, and $G_r\hookrightarrow\Delta^r$ give, respectively, that $S_r$ is Kan, its final-target map $S_r\to X_0$ is a Kan fibration, and $X_r\to S_r$ is a Kan fibration. The same applies to $d_1:X_1\to X_0$ using the first vertex inclusion.

source.place: Rezk Sections 4.1 and 5.1–5.7; agent expansion of the strict/path comparison using Kerodon 0329 and 032B (not Stacks tags)

proof.text:
Put $H_1=X_1$ and let $H_r$ be the explicit $r$-edge, $(r-1)$-path product of the homotopy-Segal definition. Its last-target map is $d_0$ on its last edge. Inductively $H_{r+1}=P(H_r\to X_0,\,d_1:X_1\to X_0)$, literally by separating the last path and edge. Define $c_r:S_r\to H_r$ by inserting all constant paths. We prove by induction that $H_r$ is Kan and $c_r$ is a weak equivalence over the last-target map. For $r=1$ both assertions follow from $H_1=S_1=X_1$. Given them for $r$, write $c_{r+1}$ as
$$S_r\times_{X_0}X_1\longrightarrow P(S_r\to X_0,d_1)\longrightarrow P(H_r\to X_0,d_1).$$
The first map is a weak equivalence by the strict/path comparison: its three objects are Kan and $d_1$ is a Kan fibration. The second is a weak equivalence by homotopy-pullback invariance applied to $c_r$, $\mathrm{id}_{X_1}$ and $\mathrm{id}_{X_0}$; the required squares commute since $c_r$ leaves the last edge unchanged. The path-comparison lemma also makes its target $H_{r+1}$ Kan. The composite inserts precisely all $r$ constant paths and leaves the last edge unchanged, completing the induction.

source.place: Rezk Sections 4.1 and 5.1–5.7; agent expansion of the strict/path comparison using Kerodon 0329 and 032B (not Stacks tags)

proof.text: By the homotopy-Segal hypothesis the consecutive-edge map $a_r:X_r\to H_r$ is a weak equivalence for $r\geq2$. In the displayed coordinates it is $c_r\circ b_r$, where $b_r:X_r\to S_r$ is strict edge restriction. Since $c_r$ is a weak equivalence, two-out-of-three in the Kan model structure makes $b_r$ a weak equivalence. Together with its Kan fibration property and the matching fibrations already proved, this gives the strict-product Segal condition and Reedy fibrancy required in the definition of a Segal space.

source.place: Rezk Sections 4.1 and 5.1–5.7; agent expansion of the strict/path comparison using Kerodon 0329 and 032B (not Stacks tags)

proof.text: For any list $\mathbf x=(x_0,\ldots,x_n)$ of vertices, put $F_n(\mathbf x)=X_n\times_{X_0^{n+1}}\{\mathbf x\}$. The all-vertices map $v_n$ is a Kan fibration and both its domain and codomain are Kan. Finite products of Kan complexes are Kan by taking a filler in each coordinate; the one-point simplicial set is Kan as well. Apply the strict/path pullback lemma to $v_n$ and $\{\mathbf x\}\to X_0^{n+1}$. It gives the constant-path weak equivalence $F_n(\mathbf x)\to T_X(\mathbf x)$, where $T_X$ is exactly the path homotopy fiber in the homotopy-Segal definition. For $n=1$ this is the asserted mapping-fiber comparison. These maps commute with restriction of a simplex and its vertex list: restriction sends a constant tuple path to the constant path at the restricted tuple, in every inner degree.

source.place: Rezk Sections 4.1 and 5.1–5.7; agent expansion of the strict/path comparison using Kerodon 0329 and 032B (not Stacks tags)

proof.text:
The degree-two map $b_2:X_2\to S_2$ is a Kan fibration and a weak equivalence, hence a trivial fibration in the Kan model structure. Its pullback over a fixed triple $(x,y,z)$ is
$$F_2(x,y,z)\longrightarrow M^{\mathrm{str}}(x,y)\times M^{\mathrm{str}}(y,z),$$
where $M^{\mathrm{str}}(x,y)=F_1(x,y)$. It too is a trivial fibration: any lifting square against a boundary inclusion is a square upstairs, and its lift has the prescribed image in the triple of vertices. In particular, lifting against $\partial\Delta^0=\varnothing\hookrightarrow\Delta^0$ shows that any two strict arrows $f:x\to y$, $g:y\to z$ admit a strict $2$-simplex $\sigma$ with consecutive edges $(f,g)$. This uses no nonempty-fiber assumption; it is an assertion for each given pair of arrows.

source.place: Rezk Sections 4.1 and 5.1–5.7; agent expansion of the strict/path comparison using Kerodon 0329 and 032B (not Stacks tags)

proof.text:
Write $j_{xy}:\pi_0M^{\mathrm{str}}(x,y)\to\pi_0M_X(x,y)$ for the bijection from the mapping-fiber weak equivalence. It sends $[f]$ to the class of $f$ with constant endpoint path. For strict arrows $f,g$, choose $\sigma$ as in the previous step. The strict composition is $[d_1\sigma]$. The constant-path image of $\sigma$ in $T_X(x,y,z)$ restricts to the constant-path images of $f,g,d_1\sigma$ under $d_2,d_0,d_1$, respectively. By the composition-graph clause of the homotopy-Segal definition, this proves
$$j_{xz}([d_1\sigma])=j_{yz}([g])\circ j_{xy}([f]).$$
Each $j$ is onto, so this verifies composition for every pair of morphisms in the path-model category. Both identities are represented by $s_0x$ with the constant endpoint path. Thus the identity on objects and the $j$ on arrows define a functor, bijective on every hom-set. Its inverse is obtained by the inverse bijections; the displayed identity proves that inverse respects composition and identities. This is an isomorphism of categories.

source.place: Rezk Sections 4.1 and 5.1–5.7; agent expansion of the strict/path comparison using Kerodon 0329 and 032B (not Stacks tags)

proof.text: For every edge $f$ of $X_1$, the category isomorphism takes its strict class to its class with constant endpoint paths and preserves and reflects invertibility. Thus the same vertices of $X_1$ represent isomorphisms in both categories. Taking their unions of components selects the identical components of the identical simplicial set $X_1$; hence the resulting simplicial subsets agree. Completeness has not been assumed or used.

split_report.summary: Expanded the proof into eight steps: arbitrary-monomorphism division yields matching, spine and all-vertex fibrations; induction compares strict and explicit path Segal products via existing Kan comparison and invariance nodes; two-out-of-three gives the strict Segal condition; all-vertex fiber comparisons commute with face restriction; a trivial-fibration lift and the explicit composition graph identify identities and composition, hence equivalence components. No new nodes, no change of statement or hypotheses.

Step 1: X->* checked against the any-monomorphism division clause. Delta^n\X is X_n with the outer coordinate first; A = empty set, the boundary and the vertex set give Kan X_n, strict Reedy matching fibrations and v_n, with v_1=(d_1,d_0). Step 2: the spine division object is S_r with d_0 matched to d_1, and the fibrations come from the stated monomorphisms. Step 3: the induction is stated explicitly. H_{r+1}=P(H_r->X_0, d_1) has the right path orientation. The first map uses path comparison (S_r, X_1, X_0 Kan; d_1 a fibration). The second uses invariance with (c_r, id, id); H_r Kan is the induction hypothesis, and H_{r+1} is Kan by the comparison node. Step 4: a_r = c_r b_r, then two-out-of-three. Step 5: P(v_n, x) is exactly T_X(x). Step 6: the fixed-triple fiber map is the pullback of the trivial fibration b_2, and lifting against the empty set into Delta^0 gives sigma. Step 7: the composition-graph clause plus the j bijections; identities are s_0 with constant paths. Step 8: the category isomorphism gives the same invertible components. proof_deps equals the union of step uses; there is no cycle; all cited nodes are in unit sk-prop-sf-biduality-general. There are no new nodes. I found no DAG duplicate, no blueprint same_as (no Segal/Reedy anywhere in main-20261015) and no Segal spaces in Mathlib (only StrictSegal). Rezk 4.1/5.1-5.7 has no archival copy (WANTED); proof_origin is agent, and the statement is consistent with Rezk's conventions. No SGA. Edge cases: empty space, discrete nerves, BG; a constant nondiscrete K is excluded by Reedy fibrancy. No fixes.
